title: The lockmark
instruction: Draw the lockmark from its master, and place it only in its four fixed places.
intro: Democracy has a structure. The lockmark draws it as nine nodes joined by links, with the lever, a larger red node at bottom right, at the place where one change moves the rest. It signs our work in four fixed places: the masthead, the page header, the footer and the sign-off.
Its drawing never changes, and it codes nothing. Chapter 11 sets how a tracker shows a bill’s steps, and words name a series or a pillar.

rules.title: Draw the lockmark from its master for its size, and keep its drawing fixed.
rules.rule: The lockmark is a three by three grid of nodes joined around its edge and through its center, with the lever in signature red at bottom right. It has four masters. Place the 16 px master from 16 to 23 px, the 24 px master from 24 to 47 px, the 48 px master at 48 px in the masthead and on covers and posters, and at exactly twice that, 96 px, in a social card’s sign-off, and the display master, drawn for our brand guide’s fifth edition, at every other size from 49 px. Each master keeps the nine nodes in the same order, their links and the lever at bottom right. The 16, 24 and 48 px masters sit on the pixel grid and draw the nodes and the lever heavier than the display master, so the drawing holds at the sizes each one serves.

why.text: At small sizes our fifth edition’s single master lost its shape: at 24 px only 5 percent of its ink was solid, and at 16 px the lever became one pink pixel. The small masters set every node and link on whole pixels and draw the lever one size up, so it still reads as the place where one change moves the rest. At 48 px the display master covers 15 percent of its field with ink, against 42 percent for the 24 px master at 24 px, so the masthead and the sign-off take a 48 px master drawn the same way, which covers 22 percent. In the 24 and 48 px masters each node and the lever is one outline on the pixel grid, so between their sizes the nodes stay whole. The 48 px master serves 48 px and exactly twice that, 96 px, where each of its pixels becomes a block of 2 by 2. At any other size its edges fall between pixels and soften.
why.basis: Our measurements, October and November 2026; the 48 px master, the rebuilt 24 and 48 px files and the 96 px sign-off on social cards approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: The lockmark’s construction at 240 px, then its four masters at true size: the display master at 96 px and the 48, 24 and 16 px masters. Last, the 48 px master on Charcoal and on Prussian.

failure.caption: Our fifth edition’s master scaled to 16 px beside the 16 px master. Its nodes shrink to the width of a link and the lever turns into a single pink pixel.

rules.builders: The lockmark files read --link for the links and --lever for the lever. Leave the lever on the signature token; on Prussian, place the White file from prussian/. Place the 48 px master on whole pixels at exactly 48 px, the size its pixel grid was drawn for, or at exactly 96 px in a social card’s sign-off. The 24 and 48 px files this rule lists draw each node and the lever as one outline; the earlier files, one rect per pixel row, stay in the folder only as the record. The display master keeps our fifth edition’s drawing, with its links held at 1 px at every size.

rules.title: Place the lockmark only in its four places, once in a view.
rules.rule: The lockmark signs four places, at the size each one sets: the masthead, where L3 sets it at 48 px beside the wordmark (Rule 03.6); the page header of a report or slide page, 24 px beside the section label; the footer, 24 px beside the tagline or 16 px beside a chart’s source line; and the sign-off at the bottom right, 96 px on a social card and 48 px on a cover or poster. Each place draws the master made for its size, and a social card draws the 48 px master at exactly twice its size, so its nodes, links and lever still land on whole pixels. A view shows the lockmark once, so when a masthead and a footer share a view, the footer keeps it.

why.text: A signature works by turning up in the same place at the same size, so a reader finds it without looking. Because each place draws a master on whole pixels, at the size it was made for or at exactly twice that, the four places read as one mark at the size each one sets. On a social card the sign-off stands at 96 px. A feed shrinks the card to 500 px wide or less, and some services then save the small copy as a JPEG that keeps color in blocks of 2 by 2 pixels. On our card at 360 px, that leaves the lever no red pixels at 48 px and 17 red pixels at 96 px. Used as a bullet or scattered as decoration, the lockmark stops signing the page.
why.basis: Design judgment, approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: The four places at true size: a 768 px site masthead with L3, its lockmark at 48 px; a report page header with the lockmark at 24 px beside the section label; a footer with the lockmark at 24 px beside the tagline, and a chart’s footer with it at 16 px beside the source line; and the bottom-right corner of a 1080 px social card with the lockmark at 96 px inside the 72 px margin.

failure.caption: The lockmark used as list bullets on a flyer, three lockmarks in one view, each one decoration.

specs.label: Masthead
specs.value: L3 on screens from 48em, 768 px at the default text size, and in the email header, from its masthead master: the 24 px wordmark master, 13 px of space and the lockmark at 48 px from its 48 px master (Rule 03.6). In print, L3’s print master, with the lockmark at the same 2.18 cap heights (Rule 03.2)

specs.label: Page header
specs.value: 24 px beside the section label on report and slide pages; 0.25 in in print

specs.label: Footer
specs.value: 24 px, then 12 px of space and the tagline, on one line at the footer’s left edge, at the foot of a page, an email or a letter; 16 px at the right end of a chart’s source line. L6, the strip that closes a report, carries it at L6’s own proportion (Rule 03.2), and a page narrower than L6’s 884 px closes with this footer

specs.label: Sign-off
specs.value: Bottom right, inside the margin. On a social card, 96 px: the 48 px master drawn at exactly twice its size, so every node, link and the lever land on whole pixels. On a cover or poster, 48 px from the 48 px master. In print, 0.50 in from the display master, since the 48 px master is drawn for a screen’s pixel grid

specs.label: Feed test
specs.value: A 1200 by 630 px card, reduced to 500 and 360 px wide, as a feed shows it, must keep a visible lockmark. On a light ground, such as Newsprint or White, each of its eight dark nodes keeps at least one near-black pixel (every color channel under 70), and the lever keeps at least four red pixels (red over 170, green and blue under 120). Reduce the card with Lanczos resampling, a common filter for shrinking images, and count each node’s square plus 1 px on every side

specs.label: Feed test, dark card
specs.value: On Charcoal, each of the eight light nodes keeps at least one block of 2 by 2 pixels with every color channel over 155, and the lever keeps at least four red pixels, counted as on a light ground. On Prussian, where the lever is White as well, each of the nine nodes keeps such a block with every channel over 190. On a dark ground the links take the nodes’ own color, and in a 96 px sign-off they run 2 px wide, so one bright pixel can come from a link; a link shrunk under 1 px cannot fill a block. Each floor sits halfway between the brightest block the links alone leave in a node’s square and the dimmest node’s brightest block, measured on our card at both widths

specs.label: Feed test, our card
specs.value: The link-preview card in the identity proofs passes with its 96 px sign-off. At 500 px wide, its lockmark keeps 8 of 8 nodes and 52 red pixels; at 360 px, 8 of 8 nodes and 22 red pixels. Drawn on White or on Charcoal, the same card keeps 8 of 8 nodes and 48 red pixels at 500 px, and 8 and 20 at 360 px. On Prussian, with the White lever counted as a ninth node, it keeps 9 of 9 at 500 px and 9 of 9 at 360 px

specs.label: Once in a view
specs.value: When a masthead and a footer share one view, the footer keeps the lockmark and the masthead sets the wordmark alone

specs.label: Favicon
specs.value: Never the lockmark: favicons use ampersand B’s 16 px master (Rule 03.4)

rules.builders: Pick the master by the size the place sets: the 48 px master for the sign-off, at exactly 96 px on a social card and 48 px on a cover or poster; L3’s masthead master, which holds it already, for the masthead on screen, and L3’s print master for a masthead in print; the 24 px master in page headers and footers; and the 16 px master in a chart’s footer. Set each on whole pixels. Run the feed test on every new template for a social card, on the file you will upload, before it ships.

rules.title: Let the lockmark code nothing.
rules.rule: Draw the lockmark the same in every place, with no node lit, dimmed, moved or added. It never shows how far a bill has moved, which series a piece belongs to or which pillar a piece serves. Each of those jobs has its own sign: chapter 11 numbers a bill’s steps, the kicker names a series in words (Rule 01.21), and a pillar takes its icon with its word beside it.

why.text: One drawing with one job is easy to learn. Our fifth edition used the same nine nodes to code a bill’s stage, a series, a pillar and a kind of content, and a reader could not tell which code a grid carried, or whether the mark in the masthead meant anything at all. Numbers and words do those jobs better, because a reader can say “step 4 of 6” out loud and words survive gray print.
why.basis: Design judgment, approved by our founder and editor in November 2026

correct.caption: A bill in a tracker list as Rule 11.5 draws it, at true size on a 358 px phone column: six numbered steps, the fourth marked as the step the bill is at, with the step in words beside them. No lockmark sits in the row.

failure.caption: The same bill drawn on the lockmark’s nine nodes, four of them filled to show progress. Nine nodes cannot count six steps, a reader has to decode the filled ones, and the mark that signs our pages changes from bill to bill.

specs.label: Drawing
specs.value: The same in every place and from each of the four masters: nine nodes in the same three by three order, their links around the edge and through the center, and the red lever at bottom right. The 16, 24 and 48 px masters draw the nodes and the lever heavier than the display master, so only the weight changes (Rule 08.1)

specs.label: A bill’s progress
specs.value: Numbered steps with the step in words; Rule 11.5

specs.label: A series
specs.value: Its name in words in the kicker; Rule 01.21

specs.label: A pillar
specs.value: Its icon with its word beside it; chapter 09

specs.label: Patterns
specs.value: None; the lockmark always appears whole

rules.builders: Take the grid out of any template that used it for a tracker, a series, a pillar or a state, and take each job from the chapter that now holds it. Chapter 11 sets the tracker’s steps, their sizes and their words, and Rule 11.5 sets them in lists.

sources: “Democracy has a structure.” is the lockmark’s explanatory line, approved by Dustin Cathcart in October 2026.
